articles.title: Los mejores descuentos del Black Friday según Ars
articles.raw_content:
Every year has a Prime Day—some years even have two Prime Days!—where we celebrate the life and achievements of the greatest leader the Autobots have ever known: the inimitable Optimus Prime. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime's bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005.

It is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and launched a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron's schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City—heroes, all of them!—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator, against which there appeared to be no defense.

And then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: "Megatron must be stopped, no matter the cost." Then the fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though the cost was high. Many brave Autobots besides Optimus Prime lost their lives during the fighting. It was truly a dark day, a black day—and so, every year on the Friday after Thanksgiving, we pause to remember the noble sacrifices made by Prime and by so many others. This is why today is known as Black Friday.

Read full article

Comments
articles.summary: El artículo presenta una parodia que mezcla la historia de Optimus Prime con la celebración del Black Friday, describiendo la jornada como un día de sacrificio y ofertas, aunque el contenido es ficticio y no ofrece información concreta sobre promociones reales.

articles.title: El drenaje de turberas representa un pequeño porcentaje del calentamiento global
articles.raw_content:
Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.

A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note.

Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don't digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO2. That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane.

Read full article

Comments
articles.summary: Un nuevo estudio del MIT cuantifica la contribución de la eliminación de turberas al calentamiento global. Los humedales de turba almacenan 600 miles de toneladas de carbono; al drenarse, liberan metano, un gas de efecto invernadero más potente que el CO₂. La investigación estima que esta práctica representa solo un pequeño porcentaje de las emisiones históricas.

articles.title: FCC aprueba despliegue de 1 millón de satélites IA de SpaceX
articles.raw_content:
In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full "constellation" of AI satellites.

The FCC's approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX's request to dispose of satellites located above 600km in space "graveyard" orbits, rather than …

Read the full story at The Verge.
articles.summary: FCC autoriza a SpaceX a desplegar hasta 1 millón de satélites equipados con chips IA bajo la iniciativa Starmind. Es la primera aprobación de una constelación completa de satélites IA. Se exige al menos un lanzamiento antes de 2033 y alcanzar el millón para 2040. La agencia pospone la eliminación de satélites sobre 600 km.

articles.title: Amazon acelera lanzamientos con SpaceX tras fallo de ULA
articles.raw_content:
A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network's build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket.

The launch was an important rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the company seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA's Vulcan rocket, Amazon's primary launch provider. Now, an Amazon official tells Ars it is accelerating several Falcon 9 launches the company has purchased from SpaceX, which also owns the Starlink satellite network that Amazon seeks to dethrone.

The next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now planned for December, Amazon said, moved forward from its previous launch date next year. Several more Falcon 9s are scheduled to launch Amazon Leo satellites in rapid succession after the December flight.

Read full article

Comments
articles.summary: Amazon ha impulsado su constelación Leo con un lanzamiento de Ariane 6, añadiendo 36 satélites tras la pérdida de 40 en el fallo del cohete Vulcan de ULA. El impulso europeo refuerza la posición de Amazon en el mercado de telecomunicaciones, mientras acelera lanzamientos Falcon 9 de SpaceX para cubrir la brecha. Esta estrategia es clave para el sector europeo

articles.title: Jensen Huang vuelve a ser CEO y presidente de Nvidia
articles.raw_content:
Nvidia's board of directors has voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman of the board, just 11 days after he resigned in the wake of multiple scandals.

The reinstatement, announced Monday morning, is "effective immediately" and was based in part on "input from senior levels of the United States government" that assured the board members that "Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk."

That assurance comes despite Huang's admitted affair with a woman who, US intelligence sources believe, was working as a Chinese spy and allegations that Nvidia had subverted export controls meant to keep Nvidia chips from reaching China. It also comes despite multiple developing investigations from multiple different government departments into those and other alleged national security, accounting, and corporate governance failures.

Read full article

Comments
articles.summary: El consejo de Nvidia ha decidido reinstaurar a Jensen Huang como CEO y presidente del consejo, tras su renuncia de hace 11 días. La decisión se basa en garantías de que su retorno no representa riesgo de seguridad nacional, pese a escándalos de relaciones personales y supuestas violaciones de controles de exportación.
